children: In the 7-year, phase III Lp(a) HORIZON trial, pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) levels by 78% in adults with elevated Lp(a) and established cardiovascular disease, but cardiovascular outcomes were unchanged. The findings are preliminary until published in a peer-reviewed journal.
The primary and extended analyses found no outcome benefit, weakening the case that lowering Lp(a) with pelacarsen reduces cardiovascular events.
The biomarker moved substantially without corresponding clinical benefit, raising uncertainty about this treatment approach.
The large international Phase III trial makes the neutral result consequential, though findings remain preliminary.
Novartis funded the trial; the release does not state the commercial or financial impact of the result.

This is a late-stage clinical readout for an investigational treatment, with the release describing the findings as preliminary. A peer-reviewed publication and updates on the three other ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials targeting Lp(a) would clarify the implications for the broader treatment approach.
Based on the original press release from American Heart Association distributed by EQS.
